note: Scripture source: the Indian Revised Version (IRV Hindi, CC BY-SA 4.0), fetched as USX from the ebible mirror (gracious-tech/fetch_collection, bibles/hin_irv/usx), all 66 books. Every mined span was sliced from that text by script, never typed. The modernised English edition quotes a modern English version; the IRV decides the Hindi wording.

Title and names agree with what the Hindi corpus already committed to: the book is सब प्रकार की शान्ति का परमेश्वर — the IRV's own wording of 2 Cor 1:3 and the title the hi faith-in-the-fire plan card (data/plan_translations/hi.json, job #1444) and the hannah-whitall-smith Hindi bio already quote; the author is हन्ना व्हिटॉल स्मिथ. This book COMPLETES the faith-in-the-fire curated plan in Hindi (he-holds-my-tomorrows.hi already ships), so seed_plans creates the hi plan row on deploy, with the prose that entry already carries; the book PR's own web build rebakes the plans pages.

Derived by measurement: a row is mined only when the translator reported the quotation verbatim AND the measurement confirms it (a 6+ character quoted segment of that block, or an 8+ character phrase in the chapter, is a byte substring of the cited IRV verse). adapted/self rows and 1 unconfirmed verbatim claim (Eph 2:14 ch06) are self_rendered. Unquoted echoes are not recorded. 413 mined, 73 self_rendered.

KJV/IRV divergences an editor should see (IRV kept inside the quotation marks unless noted): Job 13:15 'though he slay me, yet will I trust in him' — the IRV reads मुझे कुछ आशा नहीं, the opposite of the author's point, so ch12 and ch17 self-render चाहे वह मुझे घात करे, तो भी मैं उस पर आशा रखूँगा (the same wording both times); John 8:27 IRV हम से ('to us') where the KJV has 'to them' — quoted verbatim in ch04 and ch05; 2 Cor 3:18 has no 'beholding' (ch16, the one-word quote self-rendered निहारना); Josh 6:2 present tense कर देता हूँ where her argument contrasts 'I will give'/'I have given' (ch14, her contrasts self-rendered); the 'much more' verses of ch09 read क्यों न… / अधिकाई से in the IRV, so the link to the chapter's refrain is by sense; Jer 31:15 has no 'refused' — ch03 uses the IRV wording of the same text in Matt 2:18 under the Jeremiah citation; Num 32:9 'discouraged the heart' — ch13 uses the IRV's मन कच्चा कर दिया from Deut 1:28; Acts 20:24 'none of these things move me' is KJV-only (ch11, self); Jehovah-tsidkenu has no IRV transliteration (ch06 यहोवा सिदकेनू; the other compound names follow the IRV); Eph 2:14 मेल and Rom 14:17 मिलाप for 'peace' (ch06); Ps 46:5 made plural (ch12); 'the Comforter' is सहायक as the IRV has it, with one gloss शान्ति देनेवाला at its first discussion (ch03).

Citations corrected in the Hindi: ch02 Exod 3:14 → 3:13, 'Psalm 7:22-24' → 2 Sam 7:22-24, John 12:49 → 8:28, Ps 18:10 → Prov 18:10; ch04 'Zechariah 11:27' → 11:17 (chapter 11 has 17 verses). Narration corrected: ch06 'King Hezekiah' → यहोशापात (2 Chr 20); ch11 'the prophet Jeremiah' → यशायाह (the quote is Isa 28:15, 17). 'Holy Bible,' dropped from three citations (ch06). Kept as printed: ch01 cites John 20:30 for 20:30-31; ch02 b28 blends John 8:28 + 14:10 under '(John 14:10)'.

Verse consistency: three hi references are pinned as genuinely different extents — John 14:10 (ch02's English blend of 8:28 + 14:10 under one citation) and John 14:27 (ch03, ch06) and Matt 23:37 (ch08) quote the verse with the English's own ellipsis '…', so the span is not contiguous. Phil 2:13 (ch16) and John 10:11 (ch04) were brought to the IRV spans the other hi books use.

Conventions: curly quotation marks mirror the English per chapter (the English's straight ' inner quotes are dropped rather than carried); the reader addressed as तुम, God in prayer as तू; God and Christ in the singular; 'comfort' शान्ति throughout (with चैन for 'peace' in ch02's narration only, to keep them apart); chapter titles pinned across all translators.

ENGLISH SOURCE items NOT repaired (the Hindi renders the evident sense or mirrors): ch02 stray footnote letters in 2 Sam 7:22-24 ('themd', 'people,e') and 'Creden' for Cruden; ch04 'di vinely', lost emphasis italics in b37-39; ch05 Matt 7:9-11 split across b15-16 with a lowercase start, a garbled subject in b12; ch07 unbalanced quote marks (b12, b44, b49) and 'is she should'; ch09 Augustine converted 'in Rome' (Milan); ch13 Isa 41:6-7 applied to God's people (in context the idol-makers) and Num 13:30 'Caleb and Joshua'; ch16 'it is written' twice (b4) and Rom 4:17 attributed to faith; ch17 'reveals' for 'revelations' and a hymn line's grammar.
